sections.html:
Fayetteville is the seat of Fayette County, a high-plateau county of about 668 square miles north of Beckley. The New River cuts through the middle on its way to Gauley Bridge. The 2025 population estimate is 38,165, down 5.8 percent from the 2020 count, and many sellers here own a small-town house, a lot outside any municipality, or an inherited place whose heirs live out of state.

Median home value is $95,700 and home ownership runs 77.6 percent. The 2020 census counted 19,089 housing units, 13.9 percent of them vacant. Tourism around the New River Gorge National Park and Preserve brings steady visitors, with 1,811,937 recreation visits in 2024, and some owners near the park rent to guests.

The county has three magisterial districts: New Haven, Plateau and Valley. A plateau parcel and a river-town parcel can sit in different districts, so find the district name on your tax ticket.

The Fayette County Sheriff's Tax Office handles payment. The counter is staffed on weekdays, 8:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m.

  • Office: 100 Church Street, Fayetteville. Use the Church Street and Magistrate Court entrance, because the East Maple Avenue doors do not open into the tax or assessor offices.
  • Drop box: beside the East Maple Avenue tax door.
  • Mail: Sheriff of Fayette County, P.O. Box 509, Fayetteville, WV 25840. Slip in a stamped return envelope addressed to yourself if you want the receipt mailed back.
  • Phone: 304-574-4219.
  • Online: through the sheriff's search and payment site, where card payments carry a processing fee.

The postmark on your envelope is treated as the payment date.

Two payments make up the year: September 1 for the first half, March 1 for the second. Pay on or before either one and a 2.5 percent discount comes off. Miss it and the half is delinquent from October 1 or April 1, when 9 percent annual interest starts.

Fayette adds its own deadline. Taxes still open on April 30 can be published, and publication brings extra fees. Call the office for the cut-off dates on delinquent parcels.

State law then starts a longer clock. A second list of land still owing goes together by September 10. On October 31, whatever remains unredeemed is certified to the State Auditor, and the auction price cannot fall below taxes, interest and charges. You can pay the sheriff to get off the list ahead of certification, or pay the Auditor afterward as long as the sale has not happened.

Schools receive about 62 percent of what Fayette County levies, using the 2024 tax year totals.

Levying purposeTaxes levied, 2024 tax year
State$139,827

Schools$23,686,712

By property class, the levy was $9,570,546 on Class II owner-occupied homes and farms, $19,970,745 on Class III property outside municipalities and $8,671,030 on Class IV property inside them. Class III carries more than half the burden, which fits a county with a lot of land outside towns.

Your venue is the County Commission wearing its Board of Equalization and Review hat, which convenes beginning February 1. Houses are valued as of July 1 at 60 percent of true and actual value, which means the real argument is what yours would have fetched on that day.

Adjournment is allowed after February 15 and required by the end of the month. Skip the meeting and your only remaining route for that year is the Office of Tax Appeals, with a March 31 deadline. If the board wants to raise your number, it owes you five days of written notice and a chance to speak first. For real estate questions, call the assessor at 100 Church Street, 304-574-4239 or 304-574-4240.

A $20,000 cut in assessed value is available to owners aged 65 and up or permanently and totally disabled. Two consecutive calendar years of living in West Virginia is part of the test. Applications are taken from July 1 through December 1, the exemption covers a primary residence only, and anyone 64 or older can contact the assessor to get started.

If you already hold the exemption, tell the title agent when prorations come up. The exemption belongs to the claimant, so a buyer would have to qualify separately.

Heirs who live elsewhere often discover a tax ticket has been going to an old address. If that sounds familiar, call the sheriff's office on 304-574-4219 and confirm what is owed for the current and prior years before anything else. Delinquent land can be listed in September, so an unanswered ticket is the first thing to clear.

The assessor's office on Church Street can confirm the district, class and assessed value on file. With that and a payoff from the sheriff, a title agent can see the full cost of clearing the parcel. A buyer paying cash can often accept the house as it sits, which spares you from repairs or a long wait for a financed buyer to complete underwriting.

A title agent pays unpaid taxes out of the seller's proceeds, and the deed transfer carries a tax of its own. Recording the deed costs $1.10 per $500 of value. The county adds 55 cents per $500, an amount the commission is allowed to raise to $1.65, and transfers for consideration also pay a $20 fee. In the usual deal the seller covers this, though a buyer can take the deed without payment. Check with the clerk for the county's present figure.

Timing matters most when a parcel is near the April 30 publication date or the September list. A cash purchase can close in days and settle the open ticket, which keeps the property off the delinquent list.

  1. Ring the sheriff's tax office and ask for a written payoff.
  2. Pass the figure along to your title agent.
  3. At closing the agent pays the ticket from your proceeds and you get what remains.

Bring the parcel's most recent tax ticket, the deed or inheritance paperwork, and a photo ID to whichever office you visit. When the person on the deed has died, whoever is handling the estate must show authority to sign, or the title agent will not set a closing.

The county runs a hotel and motel occupancy tax through the tax department. Report and pay by the 15th of the month after the stay. Late filers owe a $15 penalty, then 2.5 percent for the first delinquent month and 1.5 percent for each additional month. Newer payments are refused until older delinquencies are cleared.

Whether a house rented to guests counts is a question for the tax department. If you have rented near the park, ask before closing so no occupancy tax balance is left behind.

faqs.q: Where do Fayette County property tax payments go?
faqs.a: The Sheriff's Tax Office, 100 Church Street in Fayetteville, or by mail to P.O. Box 509, Fayetteville, WV 25840. Call 304-574-4219, and note that online payment is available.

faqs.q: What makes Fayette County property tax delinquent?
faqs.a: The first half goes delinquent October 1 and the second April 1. After that 9 percent yearly interest accrues, and anything still open on April 30 can be published with added fees.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Fayette County house that has unpaid taxes?
faqs.a: Yes. Typically the balance plus interest is deducted from what you receive at closing. Request the sheriff's payoff figure before settling on a closing date.

faqs.q: How do I apply for the Fayette County homestead exemption?
faqs.a: Apply at the Fayette County Assessor's Office between July 1 and December 1. To qualify you must be 65 or older, or permanently and totally disabled, and only a primary residence counts.

faqs.q: What is the deadline to appeal a Fayette County assessment?
faqs.a: Board of Equalization and Review hearings open February 1 and end by February's last day. If you lose there, the Office of Tax Appeals petition is due March 31.
